$comment: Build first — most other components compose with depth-layer. See docs/3D-DEPTH-SYSTEM.md for why the tiers are shaped this way.

depth-layer.description: Background decoration layer other components compose with. Never a section on its own. Enforces the rules that keep 3D off the critical path: reserved space, poster-first loading, reduced-motion fallback, mobile downgrade.

tier.description: Inherited from the section's depth property.

aspect.description: Required. Reserves space so the layer can never shift the page.

grain-only.description: Tier 0. Tiled noise over whatever is behind. ~2KB, no layout risk. The cheapest way to stop a gradient looking like a default.

mesh-gradient.description: Tier 0. Two or three large blurred radial gradients at low opacity. Reads as atmospheric lighting. Zero bytes.

_background.image: radial-gradient(60% 60% at 20% 10%, var(--gf-color-accent) 0%, transparent 60%), radial-gradient(50% 50% at 85% 30%, var(--gf-color-surface-inverse-2) 0%, transparent 65%)

notes: Blur radius stays large — a small blur reads as a mistake, a 60px+ blur reads as lighting.

parallax-image.description: Tier 0. Background image drifting at a different rate to content, via native CSS scroll-driven animation. No JS, no scroll listener, no jank.
notes: Uses animation-timeline: view(). Browsers without support simply render it static — an acceptable degradation, not a broken layout.
Translate distance is var(--gf-depth-parallax-strength) of the container height. Subtle beats dramatic.

prerendered-video.description: Tier 1. THE DEFAULT FOR HEROES. A 3D scene modelled in Spline or Blender and rendered out as a seamless loop. Visually identical to real-time for a non-interactive hero, at ~200-500KB with no runtime and no main-thread cost.

structure.notes: This is the LCP element. Optimise it like any hero image — under 150KB.

notes: Render AV1 primary with VP9/WebM fallback, ~1600px wide, 6-10s seamless loop.
preload="none" is deliberate: the poster paints, then the video fetches. Never preload="auto".
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> the video element is not rendered at all, poster only.

shader-canvas.description: Tier 2. A single fragment shader (~5KB, no library) for animated aurora/gradient fields. Enormous perceived production value per byte.
notes: Init on IntersectionObserver, never at page load. Pause the render loop when off-screen.
Never above the fold on mobile — poster only there.

interactive-3d.description: Tier 3. Real Spline or three.js with interaction. PAID ADD-ON ONLY. Most likely thing in the library to fail the CWV gate.
notes: Lazy-load on intersection. Never in the initial bundle.
Poster stays visible until the scene is interactive.
Mobile falls back to prerendered-video. No exceptions.
Hard budget 1.5MB, and it must still pass qa/checklist.md. If it cannot, it does not ship — including when the client loves it.

responsive.base: Tier is capped at 1 below 768px regardless of the section's setting — mobile gets the poster, not the runtime.

a11y: aria-hidden="true" on the whole layer — it is decoration and must never be announced.
pointer-events: none so it cannot intercept clicks.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables every animation and prevents video/canvas from loading.

depthBehaviour.0: grain-only or mesh-gradient. No network cost.

invariants: The container ALWAYS has a reserved aspect-ratio or fixed height. This is the single rule that keeps CLS at zero.
The poster is ALWAYS the LCP candidate. A video or canvas as LCP is a build failure — qa.mjs checks this.
